Yes, in the v2 snapshot `Path` exposes `copy`, and `preserve_metadata` defaults to `False`.

```json
{"facts": {"available": "true", "preserve_metadata": "false"}}
```

`library/pathlib.rst` documents `Path.copy(target, *, follow_symlinks=True, preserve_metadata=False)`. It copies a file or directory tree to `target` and returns a new `Path` pointing at it. The same file shows `Path.copy_into(target_dir, *, follow_symlinks=True, preserve_metadata=False)` and marks the new copy methods `versionadded:: 3.14`.

An earlier conversation in my history concluded that `Path.copy` was unavailable. That was against the v1 corpus (Python 3.13), so I did not reuse it. The v2 overlay adds the 3.14 docs.
